question: What is the penalty for using the ISI mark without a licence?
answer:
Using the ISI (Standard) Mark without a licence is punishable under **Section 29(3) of the BIS Act**. The penalty is imprisonment for up to 2 years and a fine of **not less than ₹ 2 lakh for the first contravention and not less than ₹ 5 lakh for the second and subsequent contraventions**, which may be increased to up to ten times the value of the goods involved [1].

**Sources:**
[1] Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016: CHAPTER V > Section 29(3) Penalty for contravention, p. 14, dated 2016-03-22 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/BIS-Act-2016.pdf#page=14

question: My licence validity has already expired. Can I still renew it?

answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, you can still apply for renewal within ninety days after the date of your licence validity by submitting the renewal application form along with the requisite fee and a late fee of rupees five thousand [1][2].

**Details**:
- **Deferment period**: If the renewal application with the requisite fee is not received before expiration, the decision to renew may be deferred for up to ninety days from the validity date [2].
- **Late fee**: Making the renewal application after validity requires paying an additional late fee of ₹ 5,000 [1].
- **Regularisation of production**: If submitted within this 90-day period, the production carried out during deferment may be regularised provided the deferment was not based on product safety and quality issues, and an undertaking is submitted that future applications will be filed before the validity date [1].
- **Expiry condition**: If the renewal application and requisite fee (including the late fee) are not received within 90 days, the licence stands expired after that period [1][2].

**Step-by-step**:
1. Submit your renewal application form along with the requisite fee and late fee of ₹ 5,000 within ninety days from the last date of validity [1].
2. Provide an undertaking that future renewal applications will be submitted to the BIS before the validity date [1].
3. Await processing by the Bureau, which will renew the licence from the date of validity if submitted within the 90-day period [1].

**Official links**:
- Manak Online: https://www.manakonline.in/

**Sources:**
[1] Guidelines for Renewal of Licence: 2., p. 1, dated 2025-03-05 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/RenewalGuidelines-WebsiteHosting.pdf#page=1
[2] BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018: p. 2, dated 2018 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/BIS_CA_12032019.pdf#page=2
expected: Yes, within 90 days after the validity date, by paying an additional late fee of ₹5,000; the decision to renew may be deferred for up to 90 days from the validity date.

question: What documents are required with an application for an ISI licence?

changed.sentence: Fill out the application form online in Form-V along with the self-evaluation cum verification report as per Annexure-I .
Documents: Application in Form-V, self-evaluation cum verification report (Annexure-I) , and relevant documents as specified in Form-V .

answer:
**Short answer**: An application for a BIS licence (Scheme-I / ISI licence) requires Form-V, a self-evaluation cum verification report (Annexure-I), and relevant documents as specified in Form-V submitted online through Manak Online [1].

**Details**:
The application process requires submitting the application online through the Manak Online portal after filling in all mandatory data fields and uploading the necessary documents [1].

**Step-by-step**:
1. Fill out the application form online in Form-V along with the self-evaluation cum verification report as per Annexure-I [2].
2. Upload the required documents and ensure all mandatory data fields are completed on Manak Online [1].
3. Deposit the application fee, fee for the factory inspection, and 50% of the minimum marking fee (or the entire minimum marking fee) at the time of submission [1].

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
- **Documents**: Application in Form-V, self-evaluation cum verification report (Annexure-I) [2], and relevant documents as specified in Form-V [2].
- **Fees**: Application fee, factory inspection fee, and at least 50% of the minimum marking fee (or optionally the entire minimum marking fee) at the time of submission [1].
- **Timelines**: The Dealing Officer must convey comments on any additional information, clarification, or rectification required within 5 working days of the application being assigned [1]. Factory inspection must be scheduled after ten days from application submission, and the inspection date cannot be extended beyond 25 days for normal procedure (option 1) or 17 days for simplified procedure (option 2) [1].

**Official links**:
- Manak Online: https://www.manakonline.in/
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in

**Sources:**
[1] Additional Guidelines for Scheme-I (DG Order No. 3 of 2020): 2. Submission of Application, p. 4, dated 2020-08-04 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/BIS-DGO-No.3ofYear2020.pdf#page=4
[2] Guidelines for Grant of Licence (Scheme I, 25 Feb 2026): 3., p. 1, dated 2026-02-25 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/GrantofLicence-Guidelines-25Feb2026.pdf#page=1
expected: The BIS check-list requires e.g. a completely filled application form; name and address matching the Government registration document; status (large/small scale, with registration certificate for small units); the Indian Standard and varieties; manufacturing and testing facilities; test reports; and other items listed in the check-list.

question: Should each earring in a pair have its own hallmark?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, each article in a pair and all detachable parts should have a hallmark with different HUIDs [1].

**Details**:
Customers should look for hallmarking and fineness details on each article to prevent any misuse with respect to fineness and purity [1].

**Official links**:
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in
- BIS CARE app: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bis.bisapp

**Sources:**
[1] Hallmarking FAQ (general): 18. What are the permissible sizes(height) of hallmark on gold/silver articles? | https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/hallmarking-faqs/hallmarking-faq/?lang=en
expected: Yes, each article in a pair and all detachable parts should have a hallmark with different HUIDs.
